18653235
What is claimed is:
1. An apparatus for identifying abnormal biomedical features within images of biomedical data, the apparatus comprising: an image capture device configured to capture an image of biomedical data pertaining to a first patient; a processor communicatively connected to the image capture device; a memory communicatively connected to the processor, wherein the memory contains instructions configuring the processor to: receive the image of biomedical data from the image capture device; extract a plurality of biomedical features from the biomedical data; receive repository data from a medical repository as a function of the plurality of biomedical features; generate at least a distance metric as a function of the plurality of biomedical features and the repository data; and highlight at least a biomedical feature within the image as a function of the at least a distance metric; and a display device communicatively connected to the processor, wherein the display device is configured to display the at least a highlighted biomedical feature within the image.
2. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein generating the at least a distance metric comprises: generating a plurality of hypotheses by creating a plurality of labels, wherein each label of the plurality of labels represents a diagnostic feature associated with one or more hypotheses within the plurality of hypotheses; identifying at least a hypothesis from the plurality of hypotheses by matching the at least a biomedical feature of the plurality of biomedical features against at least a label of the plurality of labels; and generating the at least a distance metric as a function of the at least a hypothesis.
3. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the processor is further configured to identify within the medical repository at least a second patient associated with at least a similar distance metric; wherein:
a first set of statistical parameters are extracted as a function of the image, and at least a second set of statistical parameters are extracted as a function of at least an image associated with the at least a second patient; and identifying the at least a second patient comprises matching the first set of statistical parameters with the at least a second set of statistical parameters using a statistical model.
4. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein: the biomedical data includes at least an electrocardiogram (ECG); and the at least a biomedical feature includes at least an ECG feature identified from the at least an ECG.
5. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein: the biomedical data includes time series data; and the at least a biomedical feature includes at least a feature identified from the time series data.
6. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein extracting the plurality of biomedical features comprises: receiving feature extraction training data comprising a plurality of training images as inputs and a plurality of training biomedical features as outputs; training a feature extraction model by correlating the plurality of training images with the plurality of training biomedical features; and extracting the plurality of biomedical features from the image using the trained feature extraction model.
7. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein receiving the image of biomedical data comprises: extracting a plurality of biomedical parameters from the image of biomedical data; converting the plurality of biomedical parameters to one or more digitized signals; and transforming the one or more digitized signals into an in-silicon image.
8. The apparatus of claim 7, wherein receiving the image of biomedical data further comprises: validating the one or more digitized signals, comprising: classifying the one or more digitized signals to a plurality of preliminary parameters; and
determining an accuracy status of the plurality biomedical parameters by comparing the plurality of preliminary parameters to the plurality of biomedical parameters; and generating a quality diagnostic of the biomedical data based on the result of the validation.
9. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein highlighting the at least a biomedical feature within the image comprises generating a color-coded heat map at one or more regions within the image.
10. The apparatus of claim 9, wherein generating the color-coded heat map comprises: generating a plurality of color-coded regions as function of the at least a distance metric; and displaying, using the display device, the plurality of color-coded regions.
11. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a user interface, wherein highlighting the at least a biomedical feature within the image comprises: receiving, using the user interface, a user query from a user; and highlighting, using the user interface, the at least a biomedical feature within the image as a function of the user query.
12. A method for identifying abnormal biomedical features within images of biomedical data, the method comprising: capturing, using an image capture device, an image of biomedical data pertaining to a first patient; receiving, by a processor from the image capture device, the image of biomedical data; extracting, by the processor, a plurality of biomedical features as a function of the biomedical data; receiving, by the processor, repository data from a medical repository as a function of the plurality of biomedical features; generating, by the processor, at least a distance metric as a function of the plurality of biomedical features and the repository data; highlighting, by the processor, at least a biomedical feature within the image as a function of the at least a distance metric; and
displaying, using a display device, the at least a highlighted biomedical feature within the image.
13. The method of claim 12, wherein generating the at least a distance metric comprises: generating a plurality of hypotheses by creating a plurality of labels, wherein each label of the plurality of labels represents a diagnostic feature associated with one or more hypotheses within the plurality of hypotheses; identifying at least a hypothesis from the plurality of hypotheses by matching the at least a biomedical feature of the plurality of biomedical features against at least a label of the plurality of labels; and generating the at least a distance metric as a function of the at least a hypothesis.
14. The method of claim 12, wherein the method further comprises identifying, by the processor, within the medical repository at least a second patient associated with at least a similar distance metric; wherein: a first set of statistical parameters are extracted as a function of the image, and at least a second set of statistical parameters are extracted as a function of at least an image associated with the at least a second patient; and identifying the at least a second patient comprises matching the first set of statistical parameters with the at least a second set of statistical parameters using a statistical model.
15. The method of claim 12, wherein: the biomedical data includes at least an electrocardiogram (ECG); and the at least a biomedical feature includes at least an ECG feature identified from the at least an ECG.
16. The method of claim 12, wherein: the biomedical data includes time series data; and the at least a biomedical feature includes at least a feature identified from the time series data.
17. The method of claim 12, wherein extracting the plurality of biomedical features comprises: receiving feature extraction training data comprising a plurality of training images as inputs and a plurality of training biomedical features as outputs;
training a feature extraction model by correlating the plurality of training images with the plurality of training biomedical features; and extracting the plurality of biomedical features from the image using the trained feature extraction model.
18. The method of claim 12, wherein receiving the image of biomedical data comprises: extracting a plurality of biomedical parameters from the image of biomedical data; converting the plurality of biomedical parameters to one or more digitized signals; and transforming the one or more digitized signals into an in-silicon image.
19. The method of claim 18, wherein receiving the image of biomedical data further comprises: validating the one or more digitized signals, comprising: classifying the one or more digitized signals to a plurality of preliminary parameters; and determining an accuracy status of the plurality biomedical parameters by comparing the plurality of preliminary parameters to the plurality of biomedical parameters; and generating a quality diagnostic of the biomedical data based on the result of the validation.
20. The method of claim 12, wherein highlighting the at least a biomedical feature within the image comprises generating a color-coded heat map at one or more regions within the image.
21. The method of claim 20, wherein generating the color-coded heat map comprises: generating a plurality of color-coded regions as function of the at least a distance metric; and displaying, using the display device, the plurality of color-coded regions.
22. The method of claim 12, wherein highlighting the at least a biomedical feature within the image comprises: receiving, using a user interface, a user query from a user; and highlighting, using the user interface, the at least a biomedical feature within the image as a function of the user query.
